name: pdlc-workflows

scripts.test:coverage: c8 npm test -- --runInBand && c8 report --reporter=json && node scripts/check-wave-resume-delta-coverage.mjs && c8 report --check-coverage --per-file --branches 85 --lines 0 --functions 0 --statements 0

//c8-per-file: `test:coverage` is two stages. Stage 1 (`c8 npm test`) applies the `c8` block below in AGGREGATE. Stage 2 re-reports the same run with `--per-file`, enforcing only the floor DoD criterion 4 names — branch >= 85% — on EVERY included module (the other three are passed 0 because their aggregate floors are already enforced by stage 1; naming per-file numbers for them would mean lowering the declared 90 to orchestrate-queue.js's 77.46% functions, i.e. weakening the declaration to fit the code). Without stage 2 the block's floors are not the floors it enforces: orchestrate-dev.js is ~15k lines and dominates the aggregate, so a small module could sit under 85% branch unnoticed (CODE_REVIEW v2 §1-1).
//c8: Coverage is measured by c8, not by jest's own --coverage: under --experimental-vm-modules the modules under test are evaluated as ESM through jest's vm-module path, where babel instrumentation reports 0% for them. c8 reads V8's own coverage and sees them. The include set is the modules this feature edits (CODE_REVIEW v1 §1-2), including `scripts/check-wave-resume-delta-coverage.mjs`, which is production code on a required check and so is measured like the modules it measures (CODE_REVIEW v1 §1-1); dist/ is generated and __tests__/ is the measuring instrument, so neither is a subject. `scripts/capture-learnings-baseline.mjs` is production tooling that lives above this package, so it needs `allow-external` (c8 drops every file outside its cwd otherwise). `allow-external` also changes how the REST of the include set resolves: bare cwd-relative basenames stop matching under it, so adding the script's entry alone silently dropped orchestrate-dev.js, orchestrate-queue.js and build-runtime.mjs out of the report and left the aggregate gate measuring a 200-line script (CODE_REVIEW v1 F4, second round). EVERY entry is therefore `**/`-anchored and path-qualified, and `exclude` drops the merge-base worktrees the capture tests materialise, whose own copies of orchestrate-dev.js would otherwise match. `coverageInstrumentation.test.js` runs c8 against this block and fails if a module stops resolving.
